h1: The 6 Best Locking Filing Cabinets of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Locking File Cabinets 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six metal filing cabinets with confirmed locks, from under $50 to $200, compared on drawers, folder fit and footprint.
summary: The Letaya 3 Drawer rolling cabinet is the best overall: a confirmed lock, three drawers, legal-folder fit and no assembly. The Letaya lateral suits a wall run, and the SISESOL is the cheapest locking cabinet here. The BYNSOE only takes letter, the SteeLoong leaves folder fit unconfirmed, and the Livofloral offers the most storage with two locks.
intro: A filing cabinet lock is a privacy device, not a vault. It keeps curious kids, houseguests and cleaners out of tax returns and medical folders, and that is all a keyed cylinder at this price can promise. What the lock cannot fix is a drawer that rejects your paperwork, which is the mistake that actually sends cabinets back.

The category's quiet trap is folder fit. Letter, legal and A4 hanging folders need different drawer widths, and some listings never say which they accept. We ranked six steel cabinets whose listings confirm a lock, dropping a garage storage unit built for tools and a rolling cabinet with no confirmed lock. Scores come from the spec sheets: folder sizes, drawer count, footprint and assembly burden.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock, Under Desk Metal Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: Three locking drawers that roll under a desk, no assembly needed.
products.description:
The Letaya 3 Drawer is the cabinet to buy when the files must fit under a desk and the lock must be real. It has three drawers on caster wheels, a lock confirmed on the listing, and room for letter, legal and A4 hanging folders in a black metal body. It arrives fully assembled, which removes the usual hour of flat-pack wrestling and the racked frames that follow.

It outranks the two-drawer picks by adding a third drawer without widening the footprint, and it costs more than the SISESOL below it. The lateral Letaya trades the rolling convenience for wall-friendly width.

Home offices with little floor space will like it best. The caveat is the casters: on an uneven floor a loaded cabinet can drift, so lock the wheels once it is placed.
products.idealFor: Home offices that need compact rolling storage.
products.skipIf: You want a wall-hugging lateral layout.

products.name: Letaya 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Metal Lateral Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: A wide, low cabinet that sits neatly along a wall.
products.description:
The lateral Letaya turns the usual cabinet on its side. About 28 inches wide with two drawers, it carries a confirmed lock, takes letter, legal and A4 hanging folders, and has a sturdy top surface. Laterals put every file within a single arm reach instead of burying the back folders behind the front ones.

It takes second place behind the rolling Letaya because two drawers hold less and there are no casters, and the extra width will not slide under a desk. What you get in return is a working surface along a wall, good for a printer.

Pick it for a spare room or hallway run where the wall is free. The caveat is the footprint: measure the wall length before buying, because 28 inches of width is a commitment, and capacity stays at two drawers.
products.idealFor: Wall runs in a spare room.
products.skipIf: You need to slide it under a desk.

products.name: SISESOL 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Narrow Vertical Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: The cheapest locking cabinet here and still narrow enough for most desks.
products.description:
The SISESOL is how you get a locking cabinet for the least money. It is a narrow, two-drawer vertical design with a confirmed lock, and the listing names letter, A4 and legal fit. It slides under most desks, and it sits at the $25 to $50 mark.

It ranks third because the build is simpler than the Letaya pair: it needs assembly, and the steel feels lighter, which matters once drawers fill with paper. Still, it beats the BYNSOE below on two counts, since it accepts legal folders and costs less.

A first-time buyer setting up a home file for bills and receipts will get what they need. The caveat is weight. Heavy binders or stacked reference books in thin steel may flex the drawers, so keep loads moderate and bottom-heavy.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers on a tight budget.

products.name: BYNSOE 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Vertical Filing Storage Cabinet
products.verdict: A plain steel cabinet with a lock and letter-size drawers.
products.description:
BYNSOE builds a plain, honest steel cabinet: two vertical drawers, a lock confirmed on the listing, letter-size files only and assembly required. There is little here beyond the basics, and that is exactly the pitch. Steel construction keeps the cabinet rigid enough for ordinary household paperwork.

It sits fourth because the SISESOL listing covers letter, legal and A4 for less money, while the BYNSOE lands in the $50 to $100 bucket. The only reason to choose it is a preference for its steel build and a shape you already like.

It fits a household that files letter paper and nothing else. The caveat is blunt: legal-size documents such as some contracts and deeds will not fit, so anyone with those should pick one of the Letaya models or the SISESOL instead.

products.name: SteeLoong 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Metal Office File Cabinet
products.verdict: A compact two-drawer metal cabinet for small offices.
products.description:
SteeLoong makes the case for compact. This two-drawer metal cabinet has a confirmed lock, a black finish and a footprint kept small for tight offices. Assembly is needed. It is a no-fuss way to add a locked drawer to a small room without giving up a corner.

It ranks fifth because the listing never names the folder sizes it accepts. That one omission puts the work on you: the BYNSOE at least states letter-only, and the SISESOL spells out letter, A4 and legal. A cabinet that might fit your hanging files is a riskier buy than one that says it does.

Choose it for a small home office where floor space is short. Before ordering, check the interior drawer dimensions against your folders, because the missing fit information is the real caveat.
products.idealFor: Small home offices with little floor space.

products.name: Livofloral Vertical File Cabinet with 4 Drawers and 1 Door, 2 Locks
products.verdict: Four drawers and a door with two separate locks.
products.description:
The Livofloral is the storage heavyweight: four drawers and a lockable door in white metal, with two confirmed locks. It takes letter, legal and A4 folders, and the door section is handy for stationery or supplies you do not want in the filing drawers. Assembly is required.

It comes last because capacity comes at a footprint cost. It is tall and wide, and it lacks the track record of the Letaya cabinets that rank above it. Nothing else here stores as much, though, and two separate locks let you secure files and supplies independently.

It suits a growing paper archive in a room with space to give. The caveat is the key count: two locks mean two keys to keep track of, and a tall cabinet needs careful loading so it does not tip.

whatMatters.detail: Most cabinet locks are simple keyed cylinders. They keep children, guests and casual snoopers out but will not stop a determined thief with tools. That distinction matters when you decide what to store inside. On the listing, confirm that a lock is actually included, not just a latch, and check how many keys ship in the box.

Letter folders are the common US size, legal folders are longer, and A4 is narrower and taller. A drawer built for letter will not hold legal files, which is the number one reason cabinets get returned. Look in the title, bullets and specs for the sizes by name, and treat a listing that omits them with suspicion.

Vertical cabinets are deep and narrow, so they fit corners and under desks. Lateral cabinets are wide and shallow, so they suit wall runs and give front-to-back access to every file. The right choice depends entirely on your floor. Measure the available width and depth, and compare them with the stated dimensions before ordering.

Drawer count sets storage per square foot of floor, but taller cabinets get less stable with top drawers open. A well-designed cabinet limits how many drawers open at once and stays upright when loaded. Read the listing for an anti-tilt feature, and plan to keep heavy files in the lowest drawers.

Flat-pack cabinets take an hour or more to build and can end up slightly racked if the screws go in unevenly, which makes drawers stick. Pre-assembled models arrive ready to use. The listing states which you are buying, so check it, and if assembly is needed allow time and a second person for the frame.

faq.a: They deter casual access by children, visitors or cleaners, not a determined break-in with tools. A cabinet like the Letaya 3 Drawer keeps paperwork private at home, but irreplaceable documents belong in a fireproof safe as well.
Ignoring folder size. The BYNSOE only takes letter, so legal hanging files will not fit, while the SISESOL and both Letaya models list legal and A4 as well. Check sizes by name before you order.

faq.q: Is a lateral cabinet worth it?
faq.a: If you have a free wall, yes. The lateral Letaya gives easy reach to every folder and a flat top for a printer, but its 28 inch width does not slide under a desk like the vertical SISESOL does.

Flat-pack models like the SISESOL, BYNSOE, SteeLoong and Livofloral typically take about an hour, longer if you work alone with the taller Livofloral. The Letaya 3 Drawer arrives fully assembled, so you only need to unpack it.

faq.q: How do I stop a cabinet tipping?
faq.a: Open one drawer at a time and keep heavy files in the lowest drawers. A tall cabinet such as the Livofloral should be anchored to the wall, because loaded top drawers shift the center of gravity forward.

faq.q: What if I lose the key?
faq.a: Contact the seller for a replacement key, quoting the model and any number stamped on the lock. Keep a spare in a separate safe place, since the Livofloral has two locks and so needs two keys tracked.

finalTake: Buy the Letaya 3 Drawer if the cabinet will live under a desk, the Letaya lateral if you have a wall to fill, and the SISESOL if budget rules. Skip the BYNSOE unless you only file letter paper, and measure the SteeLoong's drawers before ordering. The Livofloral earns its footprint only when your archive keeps growing.
